evals.prompt: design a self-service flow for provisioning databases
evals.expected_output: Tiers requests by blast radius rather than resource type, auto-approves within baked-in guardrails like size limits, allowed regions, and budget caps enforced by policy-as-code, and requires a cost estimate plus owner/cost-center tag to be shown before the request can be submitted.

evals.prompt: developers keep going around the portal and using the aws console directly
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses this as the self-service path not being the path of least resistance, and recommends locking down direct provisioning access so any provisioning outside the flow requires an explicit, logged break-glass exception instead of a standing credential.

evals.prompt: let's require manual approval on every infrastructure request to stay safe
evals.expected_output: Pushes back that requiring sign-off on low-risk, repetitive requests turns approval into rubber-stamped theater, and recommends defaulting to auto-approve within guardrails while reserving human review only for production data stores, compliance boundaries, or requests above a cost threshold.
